title: $D^b_{ctf}=D^b_c$ for integral and rational coefficients
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside it, with valuation ring $\cO_E$. Use the condensed coefficient rings of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], pulled back to the small pro-étale site. Let $X$ be a qcqs scheme and $\Lambda\in\{\mathbf Z_\ell,\cO_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\Qlb\}$. Then:

1. every constructible $\Lambda_X$-module has Tor amplitude in $[-1,0]$, and in $[0,0]$ if
   $\Lambda$ is a field;
2. every $K\in\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ with cohomology in $[a,b]$ has Tor amplitude in $[a-1,b]$;
   hence $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)=\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ and
   $\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))=\Loc(\Dbc(X,\Lambda))$.

The following counterexamples are over the scalar ring, or as constant sheaves on $X=\operatorname{Spec}k$ for a separably closed field $k$. For scalar complexes, perfect means isomorphic to a bounded complex of finitely generated projective modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]; for the constant-sheaf examples, perfect means locally isomorphic to such a complex of finite projective $A_X$-modules. For a finite nonregular ring the condition is essential: $\mathbf F_\ell$ over
$\mathbf Z/\ell^2$ is constructible but has infinite projective dimension. Finite Tor
amplitude is a condition on the whole complex: for $A=\mathbf Z/\ell^2$ the complex
$[A\xrightarrow{\ell}A]$ is perfect, whereas its nonzero cohomology modules are
$\mathbf F_\ell$, which are not perfect. So for every qcqs scheme $X$ and every finite commutative ring $A$
(with its discrete condensed structure), $\Dctf(X,A)$ is thick, but it need not be stable
under standard truncations (already for $A=\mathbf Z/\ell^2$ and $X=\operatorname{Spec}k$).

proof.text: Scalar algebra. Put $R=\Lambda(*)$. Evaluation on the singleton in [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed] gives $R=\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E$, or $\Qlb$. The integral rings are discrete valuation rings by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], including $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$. For a finitely presented $R$-module $P$, choose a surjection $R^n\twoheadrightarrow P$. Over a discrete valuation ring its kernel $T\subseteq R^n$ has a basis of at most $n$ elements by [lem-sc-dvr-saturation-line-smith-normal-form]. Thus $0\to R^m\to R^n\to P\to0$ is exact for some finite $m$. Over a field, take a spanning subset of the given finite generating set minimal under inclusion. Any nontrivial dependence lets one solve for an element with nonzero coefficient, contradicting minimality. It is therefore a finite basis and $P\cong R^r$. This includes $P=0$ and rank zero.

source.place: Proof, scalar-ring sentence and Local models, finite free resolution

proof.text: Pass the integral exact sequence from step 1 to constant sheaves on any scheme $V$. This preserves exactness: the constant-sheaf functor is inverse image for the structural morphism to the point topos, so [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact] applies, with no finiteness assumption on the ring. By clause 1 of [det-prop-integral-criterion-constant-coefficients], $R_V\to\Lambda_V$ is flat for $R=\mathcal O_E$, and also for $R=\mathbf Z_\ell$ by taking $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$. Scalar extension therefore yields $0\to\Lambda_V^m\to\Lambda_V^n\to\Lambda_V\otimes_R P\to0$. In the field case scalar extension of $P\cong R^r$ gives $\Lambda_V\otimes_R P\cong\Lambda_V^r$ directly; no assertion that the ring sheaf $\Lambda_V$ is itself a field is used. Hence each finite constant local model of [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model] has a flat resolution in degrees $[-1,0]$, or a free model in degree zero for field coefficients.

source.place: Proof, Local models, exact scalar extension and finite constant local models

proof.text: The finite free sheaves in step 2 are flat: tensoring with $\Lambda_V^r$ is the finite direct-sum functor $N\mapsto N^r$, which preserves exact sequences, by the definition [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. The bounded flat resolution is K-flat by [lem-pc-kflat-closure]. Derived tensor may be computed by resolving one factor, by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Therefore for any module sheaf $N$ on $V$, its tensor with the integral model is the complex $[N^m\to N^n]$ in degrees $[-1,0]$, while with a field model it is $N^r$ in degree zero. Its cohomology vanishes outside the indicated interval. This proves the local-model amplitude calculation.

source.place: Proof, Local models, computation of the derived tensor

proof.text: Cover locality. For a pro-étale covering $\{V_i\to T\}$, [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies the small sites of its members with the slice sites. Restriction to a slice is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], and it commutes with derived tensor by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-restriction]. If a sheaf $F$ restricts to zero on the cover, then for any site object $W\to T$ its restriction is zero on $W\times_TV_i$, which cover $W$; the uniqueness part of the sheaf axiom forces every section of $F(W)$ to be zero. Thus these restrictions are jointly conservative on sheaves. Exactness gives $H^q(C)|_{V_i}=H^q(C|_{V_i})$. Apply this to $C=M\otimes^{\mathbf L}N$, separately for every $N$, to conclude that the common Tor interval in step 3 holds on any scheme where $M$ has a finite constant local model. The same argument applies to an open cover and to any fixed tensor product complex.

Prepare the strata induction. Let $I=[-1,0]$ for integral coefficients and $I=[0,0]$ for field coefficients. Prove the claim for all qcqs schemes and all constructible modules with a chosen partition into at most $n$ strata, simultaneously, by induction on $n$. The case $n=0$ is the empty scheme, on which all module sheaves vanish. For every $n\geq1$, use the following open--closed argument, also when the sole stratum has the whole underlying space but a different scheme structure [def-constructible-stratification]. The finite locally closed constructible partition and the local models on its strata are supplied by [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. For $n\geq1$ and $x\in T$, let $S$ be its stratum. The stratum immersion $Z_S\to T$ factors as a closed immersion into an open subscheme $O\subseteq T$ containing $S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-open-restriction] every stratum meets $O$ in a constructible subset of $O$, and it is still locally closed, so the strata restrict to a finite locally closed constructible partition of $O$. By [lem-sf-constructible-partition-local-closed-stratum] applied to $O$, choose an affine open $W\subseteq O$ with $x\in W$ such that $Z=S\cap W$ is closed in $W$, every $S_\nu\cap W$ is locally closed and constructible in $W$, and $U=W\setminus Z$ is quasi-compact. Give $Z$ the restriction $Z_S\times_TW$ of its stratum structure; since $W\subseteq O$, its immersion into $W$ is closed. Then $Z$ is affine and $U$ is qcqs (an open of the affine $W$, with the stated quasi-compactness). On $Z$, the restriction of $M$ still has a finite constant local model; on $U$, the other strata restrict to a partition with at most $n-1$ nonempty strata, which are locally closed and, by [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-open-restriction] for the open $U\subseteq W$, constructible in $U$; their immersions are the base changes $Z_{S_\nu}\times_TU\to U$. Restrict their covers and presentations; by clause 1 and the final paragraph of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], coefficient sheaves are identified by the canonical inverse-image isomorphism and module pullback is the corresponding exact inverse-image lift. Hence $M|_Z$ has interval $I$ by steps 2--4 and $M|_U$ has interval $I$ by the induction hypothesis. This uses the number of strata, not Noetherian induction and not an assumed globally open stratum.

source.place: Proof, Strata; corrected local induction replacing the unsupported open-stratum choice

proof.text: Detect the vanishing on $W$. Write $j:U\hookrightarrow W$, $i:Z\hookrightarrow W$, and let $N$ be any $\Lambda_W$-module. Set $C=(M|_W)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Lambda_W}N$. By the final paragraph of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], the module pullbacks $j^*,i^*$ are exact, so are their own derived functors and commute with cohomology. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], $j^*C=(M|_U)\otimes^{\mathbf L}j^*N$ and $i^*C=(M|_Z)\otimes^{\mathbf L}i^*N$. Step 5 gives $j^*H^q(C)=i^*H^q(C)=0$ for $q\notin I$. Apply the short exact sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] to the sheaf $H^q(C)$: its two outer terms $j_!j^*H^q(C)$ and $i_*i^*H^q(C)$ are zero, hence $H^q(C)=0$. Its hypothesis is met because $j$ is the quasi-compact open from step 5. This proves interval $I$ on each $W$, and step 4 for the open covering by these $W$ proves it on $T$. The induction closes, proving clause 1. This is the open--closed detection form of the blueprint's strata argument; it requires no additional derived projection formula.

source.place: Proof, Strata; open--closed detection of the tensor cohomology

proof.text: Complexes. For $K$ with constructible cohomology supported in $[a,b]$, induct on $b-a$. If $K$ is zero the assertion is immediate. If $a=b$, [lem-sf-derived-concentrated-single] identifies $K$ with $H^a(K)[-a]$, which has interval $[a-1,a]$ by clause 1 and the shift rule of [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude]. For $a<b$, take the truncation triangle $K'\to K\to K''\to K'[1]$ of [lem-sf-derived-truncation-triangle] at $b$. The long exact sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] gives $H^q(K')=H^q(K)$ for $q<b$, zero otherwise, and $H^q(K'')=0$ unless $q=b$, with $H^b(K'')=H^b(K)$. Thus $K'$ has constructible cohomology supported in $[a,b-1]$ and $K''\cong H^b(K)[-b]$ by [lem-sf-derived-concentrated-single]. Induction gives interval $[a-1,b-1]$ for $K'$ and clause 1 gives $[b-1,b]$ for $K''$. Enlarge both intervals to $[a-1,b]$ and use the extension rule of [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude]. This proves clause 2, including complexes whose extreme cohomology happens to vanish.

source.place: Proof, Complexes; base case and full truncation induction

proof.text: By [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude], $\Dctf$ is the full subcategory of $\Dbc$ satisfying finite Tor amplitude. Step 7 shows every object of $\Dbc$ satisfies this extra condition, so the two full replete subcategories have the same objects and morphisms. The defining intersections for their localizing closures in [det-def-localizing-closure-existence] therefore have identical indexing collections and are equal as well. No compactness or Brown representability assertion is needed.

source.place: Proof, Complexes, equality of categories and localizing closures

proof.text: Finite-ring thickness. For a finite commutative ring $A$, a finitely presented scalar module is a finite set, and conversely a finite module has a finite presentation: take finitely many generators and then all elements of the finite kernel in a finite free module. Thus finite constant local models are exactly finite locally constant modules, so the constructibility notion agrees with that in [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-sheaf-origin]. By that equivalence and the exact classical-sheaf equivalence [sk-thm-pe-classical-sheaves], constructible pro-étale modules are the corresponding classical sheaves. The classical subcategory is closed under kernels, cokernels and extensions by [det-pe-classical-derived-weak-serre]; exactness and full faithfulness of the equivalence identify these operations with those on the étale side. Apply [thm-constructible-serre] there, and then the constructible-origin equivalence, to obtain the same three closure properties on the pro-étale side. The constructibility notion in [prop-weil-pbc-module-bounded-constructible-triangulated] also agrees here: a constant-matrix presentation is a finite presentation, and conversely the finitely many entries of a local presentation matrix over the constant ring sheaf $A$ become constant on a common cover, so its cokernel has a finite constant local model. Hence that theorem applies with the closure properties just proved. A direct summand of bounded constructible cohomology is constructible, since it is the kernel of $1-e$ for the corresponding idempotent $e$; its cohomological bound is unchanged. Consequently $\Dbc(X,A)$ is thick, and its intersection with the thick subcategory of finite-Tor complexes, as described in [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude], shows that $\Dctf(X,A)$ is thick. This argument needs no regularity of $A$.

source.place: Statement, final thickness clause; Proof, The examples, with the finite-coefficient Serre inputs made explicit

proof.text:
The examples. Take $A=\mathbf Z/\ell^2$, $F=A/\ell A=\mathbf F_\ell$ and a point $X=\operatorname{Spec}k$ with $k$ separably closed. In $A$, $\ker(\ell:A	o A)=\ell A=\operatorname{im}(\ell:A	o A)$, while $\ker(A	o F)=\ell A$. Thus the augmented periodic free resolution $\cdots\xrightarrow{\ell}A\xrightarrow{\ell}A	o F	o0$ is exact. Passing to constant sheaves preserves exactness by [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact]. It is bounded above and flat, hence K-flat by [lem-pc-kflat-closure]; using the one-factor computation of derived tensor in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], tensor with $F$ gives the complex with term $F$ in every nonpositive degree and all differentials zero. Therefore $\operatorname{Tor}^A_q(F,F)=F
e0$ for every $q\ge0$. A finite projective resolution would force these groups to vanish above its length (projective modules are direct summands of free modules, so are flat), a contradiction. Thus $F$ has infinite projective dimension and infinite Tor amplitude, although its constant sheaf is constructible: it has one stratum and the finite presentation $A\xrightarrow{\ell}A	o F	o0$ of [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. The two-term complex $P=[A\xrightarrow{\ell}A]$ in degrees $[-1,0]$ is itself a bounded finite free complex, hence perfect by [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex] over the scalar ring and by the same constant finite free model on the site; it is K-flat and has Tor amplitude $[-1,0]$ by the same calculation as step 3. Its cohomology is $\ell A\cong F$ in degree $-1$ (send $ ar a\mapsto\ell a$) and $A/\ell A=F$ in degree zero. The cohomology module $F$ is not perfect: a bounded complex $Q$ of finitely generated projective $A$-modules is a bounded complex of flat modules, so $H^{-q}(Q\otimes_AF)=0$ for $q$ large, against $\operatorname{Tor}^A_q(F,F)
e0$. Likewise the constant sheaf $F$ is not locally perfect: on a nonempty member $V$ of a cover the same calculation gives $H^{-q}(F_V\otimes^{\mathbf L}F_V)=F_V
e0$ for all $q\ge0$, whereas a bounded complex of finite projective (direct summands of finite free, hence flat) $A_V$-modules is K-flat by [lem-pc-kflat-closure] and gives bounded cohomology. Thus $P\in\Dctf(X,A)$ but $	au_{\ge0}P\cong F$ and $	au_{\le-1}P\cong F[1]$ have infinite Tor amplitude, by the shift rule of [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude]. This proves the asserted failure of stability under standard truncations, compatibly with step 9.

source.place: Proof, The examples; periodic resolution, perfect complex, and explicit truncations
